text:
Evelyn: Morning all — quick executive weekly. Three signal items + metrics + asks.

1) SLA & policy changes
- We are introducing a two-tier SLA for Dedicated customers: Standard (99.9% uptime) and Foundational (99.95% uptime). Details in the doc linked below. Grace window for existing contracts: 90 days.
- Why: predictable capacity demand + clearer packaging for enterprise sales.
- Immediate ask: Eng/Product, help confirm rollback policy for capacity degradations by EOD Fri.

2) Data retention tweak for EU Private beta
- Shortening default request log retention from 180d -> 90d for EU regions, opt-in extended retention behind an enterprise add-on. This is to align with some partner legal asks and reduce storage costs.
- Security/Compliance: Kait, please post the audit checklist and any blockers.

3) Performance & cost play: 'BatchFirst' default config
- Ops/Runtime will flip the default autoscaler/batching profile for new Dedicated clusters to BatchFirst (aggressive batching, slightly higher median latency, ~12-18% token cost improvement).
- Canary plan: 2-week canary on non-SLA tier, then expand.
- Ask: Sales/CS, flag any customers that must be excluded from this default (we will respect pinned configs).

Metrics snapshot (last 7 days vs prior 7d):
- Avg token cost per 1k: $0.82 -> $0.72 (down 12%)
- P95 latency (text gen hosted): 210ms -> 235ms (up 12%)
- Dedicated utilization: 68% -> 76% (improved efficiency)

Launch readiness: runtime v0.9 (attention optimizations + quantization path) is scheduled for canary next Tues 09:00 PT. This release includes two breaking config toggles (KV cache eviction and default quant profile). Docs + migration guide in #docs.

Action items / owners (short):
- Marco: finalize rollback & capacity policy (due Fri EOD).
- Priya: update pricing page to show new SLA tiers + notify sales enablement (due Tue).
- Kait: publish EU audit checklist + retention exception flow (48h).
- Jules: financial impact note on BatchFirst (quick model by Wed).
- Ops: start canary for BatchFirst on Mon, watch cost/latency dashboards.

Link: https://intranet.redwood/integration/exec-weekly/5112345678 (details + docs) :rocket:

Evelyn: Quick ask to managers — keep one-line status in your team channels on Friday so we can compile a rollup for Monday leadership. :eyes:

Marco: Got it. Working on rollback doc now. My immediate question: for canary, do we prefer region-scoped or customer-scoped testing?

Evelyn: Marco — prefer customer-scoped where possible. Pick a mix: 70% region-scoped traffic, 30% opt-in customers we already flagged as tolerant.

Priya: Will update the pricing page. FYI sales asked for a one-pager that explains the tradeoffs (latency vs cost) — I'll draft and share by Tue morning.

Jules: Running numbers on BatchFirst. Preliminary: if adoption hits 50% on Dedicated, ARR uplift through margin savings could be ~1.3M annually. Need more detailed cohort breakdown.

Kait: Publishing audit checklist in 2hrs. Note: for EU retention reduction we must surface the opt-in contract clause — legal will need to sign off on the wording.

OpsBot: Deploybot: canary for runtime v0.9 scheduled -> 2026-03-31T16:00:00Z (canary id: can-511234).

Marco: For rollback policy — proposing an automatic fallback to previous model variant on error rate >1% sustained for 5m, and manual operator rollback for perf regressions. Sharing draft in #eng-runtime.

Evelyn: Love that. Keep the thresholds conservative for the first month.

Priya: Quick note — we'll also add an eval job to the CI that runs our core prompt set against v0.9 before canary flip. Saves us surprises.

Evelyn: Thanks team. One more: hiring update — we are opening two senior infra roles to help scale Dedicated ops. Please nominate internal referrals.

Marco: Will circulate job briefs.

Evelyn: That's it from me. Short check-in Fri 11:00 PT.

Priya: :thumbsup:

Jules: :moneybag: (will follow up with a spreadsheet)

Kait: :lock: checklist posted.

Evelyn: Closing — appreciate the fast turn.
